budget_items.what_was_said: Warrants covering March 3-12, 2025 were presented to the committee for review.
A Lunenburg family donated to the Turkey Hill Elementary music department, to be deposited into a gift account.
A citizen-petitioned warrant article would raise and appropriate this amount to supplement the FY26 schools budget, contingent on passage of a Proposition 2½ ballot question.

budget_items.topic: Level-service budget vs. town manager's budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The override figure was calculated as the difference between the level-service school budget and the town manager's proposed school budget.

budget_items.topic: High school contracted services line transfer
budget_items.what_was_said: Funds from the high school supply line and unused English textbook money were used to zero out a deficit in the contracted services line.

An unusually high need for outside/independent evaluations this year is being covered by transferring from special ed and ACE program supply lines and the home hospital tutoring account; staff called it a fluke year.
Unused supply-line money is being pooled to buy paper and cleaning supplies districtwide; a member questioned whether this cost will keep rising next year.
This line is just beginning to run negative due to McKinney-Vento (homeless student) transportation situations; staff want to watch it before transferring more funds.
A proposed raise schedule for unaffiliated staff, mostly revolving-fund-paid Extended Day/ELC employees, was presented as 4% the first year and 2.5% in each following year.

budget_items.topic: Net position changes over five years
budget_items.what_was_said: After accounting for FY25 and FY26 cuts, the district will have lost more positions than it added over the past five years, leaving staffing lower than when the superintendent arrived.
The athletic director proposed splitting camp revenue with half going to staff running the camps and half into the athletics revolving account.
This amount was previously removed from the athletics revolving account when the secretary position was cut; restoring the position depends on the revolving account's health and camp revenue.

If Mrs Brzozowski cannot attend a final superintendent-screening decision meeting after March 31, she will leave her interview rubric/recommendation with the MASC representative to share with the rest of the screening committee.
Agreed to use the school department's email to invite families to write letters to state legislators about school funding, with guidance on tone and including name/address.
Agreed the chair would revise the draft state-funding letter to emphasize that current FY26 state budget proposals are stopgap measures, not a long-term fix.

minutes.headline: Committee reviewed FY26 cuts leaving fewer staff than five years ago while a citizen override heads to the ballot.
minutes.summary: The committee heard emotional public comment against staffing and program cuts and a student's testimony on special education support, then worked through routine FY26 business: budget transfers, grants, handbooks, the school calendar, an athletic camp pilot, and a new unaffiliated salary schedule, all passing on roll-call votes. Much of the discussion centered on a citizen-petitioned override on the ballot, frustration over repeated town budget presentations, and the superintendent search timeline, with no vote taken on the override itself.</summary>

what_happened.line: A citizen-petitioned override that would add funding to the FY26 schools budget, contingent on a townwide ballot vote, was discussed at length with no vote taken on the override itself.
The committee was told that after FY25 and FY26 cuts, the district will have fewer staff positions than it had five years ago.
The committee voted to accept the FY25 quarterly budget report and the line item transfers that go with it.
Public comment opposed a proposed administrator cut at the high school and a proposed cut to fifth grade music, and a student described how special education support helped him.
The committee also voted to accept a multi-year salary schedule for unaffiliated staff and the FY26 school calendar.

why_it_matters: The override is a Proposition 2 1/2 ballot question that would raise additional funds for the schools budget beyond the town manager's proposal; a yes or no vote will fall to town voters.
The staffing comparison speaks to what programs and support the district can offer next year, including the special education and music positions named in public comment.
The quarterly transfers move existing appropriated funds between budget lines and do not change the total amount raised.
